dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Are you here for a tour? It's nice that you're interested in tea, and you'll learn all about it here!

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: This is the Qiaoying Village tea workshop. Most of the tea leaves are sent here after being picked.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: You might not realize that tea leaves require several processes and careful handling before they can be used to make tea.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Simply put, we need to remove the excess moisture in the leaves to deepen their fragrance and make them easier to store.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Our workshop's in charge of sunning, baking, and then stirring them in a pan.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Some types are then taken back by the tea farmers for additional processing, such as piling and fermenting.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: If you have time, you should stay in the village for a month or so. That way, you can see the full process, from leaf picking to the moment the tea's served up on tables.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the machine in that room over there?

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Ah, you're asking about the stirring machine, yes? Compared to our village's history, the machine is very young.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: We used to use a huge tea cauldron for stirring. They said it was an adeptal mechanism of some sort...

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: The traditional process creates a traditional flavor, but we must also meet the quantity demands, so these days our workshop uses new, faster machines.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: That said, with higher efficiency and more heat, the need to ensure quality is even greater.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: That's why people like me, with more than thirty years of experience, are needed to make sure things don't go wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: As for Ding Jr... He's got another decade of buckling down and learning this craft ahead, that's for sure...

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Farewell! Come back when you have time. Who knows, maybe you'd be interested in becoming one of us!
